text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000395 bills 99215 at roughly five times the complexity-adjusted expectation, and returned charts support the billed levels, but heavy note duplication leaves open whether that documentation reflects the visits.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with no chronic conditions (e.g., C0230342, C0230479 and C0230617, billed with only Z09 follow-up codes). That points to a practice-wide billing habit rather than a sicker panel alone, even though the share rises appropriately with complexity. Against this, none of the documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level, including low-complexity C0230331, recorded at high MDM and 54 minutes, which is consistent with legitimate complexity. However, about 43% of returned notes were flagged as duplicates and 13% for repeated times, and no audit trail was received, so the supporting notes could be templated or cloned rather than independent evidence. A reviewer should first obtain the EHR audit trail and compare the flagged duplicate notes for cloned text. Next, pull full charts for the zero- and one-condition 99215 claims, starting with C0230255, which also carries a problems flag, to test whether the high MDM is clinically credible."}
